html:
I was listening to an episode of the Chinese podcast Mostly Harmless, part of its “City Survival Guide” series, about Harbin, and the hosts recommended a whole stack of books about Northeast China. This was one of them.

In April I took my parents to Barcelona and brought this book along, and I couldn’t put it down. I read it whenever I had a spare moment; on the flights there and back I didn’t sleep, just kept reading. I finally finished it after we got home.

The Northeast the book describes resonated with me deeply, even though I’ve never lived in Shenyang, and even though I’m not of the same generation as its protagonists. Which says something, indirectly, about how Northeastern culture carries on unbroken from one place to the next, and about how little Northeastern society has progressed in all these years.
